domain_label: Knitwear Quality-Control Technology: Own-Demand-Buy Boundary for a Micro D2C Brand
purpose: A session-bounded method for the owner of a small AI-designed D2C acrylic/blend knitwear brand (yarn sourced in Ludhiana, sold in California/Turlock) to decide which QC technology to own, which to demand of suppliers via the purchase order, and which to buy as a third-party service: it pins the dominant defect-and-return risk per construction, separates the three layers where QC happens (yarn evenness, knit-fabric defects, finished-garment tests), grades the owner's 'thread-checker' idea into a don't-build sensor plus a cheap buildable code-back loop, holds AI vision QC to a binding dataset-transfer caveat, and hardens the QC system into an AQL-plus-lab-spot-check gate the brand actually owns, with every money/performance/throughput claim tagged FACT, ESTIMATE, or UNKNOWN.
assumptions: no per-supplier QC dataset or lab quote is supplied; cost, throughput, and accuracy bands are reasoned estimates keyed to the quality_checker deep-dive and yarn deep-dive, not invoices

the base case is an acrylic and acrylic-blend mainstream-to-premium sweater line (Ludhiana's base fibre), fully-fashioned-and-linked or cut-and-sew, sold D2C in California where pilling is the #1 post-purchase return driver
the brand owns design, brand, US import, and incoming inspection only; spinning, knitting, and lab metrology live on supplier floors and are demanded via the PO, not owned
USTER TESTER 6 list price is never published and is held as a wide estimate; the don't-own conclusion is insensitive to the exact number
any QC cost or per-piece job-work rate stated is a labeled estimate or an explicit UNKNOWN blocker, never a fabricated precise figure
off-paper-economy effects in the Ludhiana cluster are treated as a structural mechanism described generally, never as a named-party accusation, with amounts UNKNOWN
exclusions: yarn fibre selection, count/twist engineering, and spinning process (covered by the yarn fibre-line and yarn quality-spec KBs)
the unit-economics landed-cost model and the dollar recurring-QC line beyond naming it as a feed to the cost model
finishing and post-treatment chemistry (anti-pill finish application, milling, mercerising) beyond the pilling-grade acceptance test that judges it
trade/duty/HTS classification beyond the fibre-composition test that guards the duty declaration
brand marketing, consumer-facing digital-product-passport traceability strategy beyond distinguishing it from the supplier-accountability loop
AI garment design (Flux) and sampling logistics beyond naming pre-production samples as the validation substrate for vision accuracy
source_description: reasoned estimate-and-fact knowledge units for knitwear QC technology, grounded in the quality_checker sector deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md sec 1-9: the three-layer own/demand/buy model, the contractual yarn spec, incoming AQL, finished-garment lab tests, the four-layer thread-checker verdict, the AI-vision dataset-transfer caveat, the cheapest-first sequence, and the eight open questions) and the yarn deep-dive (the ~$1-2.50/garment yarn input that settles the own-vs-demand economics and shared open questions); plus the sweater-vertical SCOPE_GLOSSARY vocabulary for USTER percentiles, CVm%, IPI, hairiness, pilling grade, AQL, linking, and construction terms; no supplied QC dataset or lab quote
source_citation: Sweater-vertical Quality-Checker Deep-Dive (FACTORY/sweater_vertical/analysis/quality_checker/DEEPDIVE.md sec 1-9, reconciled.md); Yarn Deep-Dive (analysis/yarn/DEEPDIVE.md, ~$1-2.50/garment yarn input, shared open questions); SCOPE_GLOSSARY.md sec 5 (USTER STATISTICS percentiles, CVm%, U%, IPI, thin/thick/nep, hairiness H/S3, tenacity, count-CV, pilling grade 1-5, 4-point fabric inspection, AQL) and sec 3 (linking vs mock-linking vs overlock); Uster Technologies USTER STATISTICS methodology and USTER TESTER 6 / USTER QUANTUM datasheets [FACT for equipment class, price band ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN]; ISO 12945-1 pilling box, ISO 2859-1 / ANSI-ASQ Z1.4 AQL [FACT for standards]; TILDA/woven-jacquard CV-defect-detection accuracy figures cited as dataset-specific [FACT that reported, ESTIMATE that they do not transfer untested]; EU ESPR digital-product-passport regulatory trend [FACT]; heuristic estimates where no QC dataset or lab quote is supplied

competency_questions.question: For this brand's specific construction and fibre, what is the dominant defect-and-return risk the QC plan must protect against first?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEFECT_RISK_PROFILE names the dominant return driver from the deep-dive (pilling for acrylic/blend), ranks the other knit and yarn defects (holes, dropped stitches, barre, shade mismatch, skew, seam/linking failures) by return risk and likelihood, and ties each to the layer where it is caught

competency_questions.question: What are the three layers where QC happens, who owns the machine at each, and what is the brand's move at each layer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QC_LAYER_MODEL separates yarn-evenness (spinner-owned, demand), knit-fabric-defect (knitter-owned, demand-then-explore), and finished-garment (brand-owned, run) layers and assigns the own/demand/buy posture per layer

competency_questions.question: What numeric yarn-quality clause goes into the purchase order so the brand's QC starts as a contract number, not a machine?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PO_YARN_SPEC_CLAUSE states the CVm%, IPI, hairiness ceiling, tenacity/elongation floor, count plus count-CV tolerance, and fibre-composition ratio demanded, anchored to a USTER percentile tier (<=25% USTER for mainstream-to-premium acrylic) with the rationale for not over-tightening

competency_questions.question: What is USTER TESTER 6, why is it demanded-not-owned, and how does the brand obtain the certificate it produces?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: USTER_TESTER_LAB describes the off-line lab evenness tester (CVm%/IPI/hairiness/count-CV/tenacity graded against USTER STATISTICS), holds its price as a six-figure estimate/UNKNOWN, and routes the certificate from the spinner or a paid third-party lab when the micro-spinner cannot self-test

competency_questions.question: What is the in-line yarn clearer (USTER QUANTUM) and why does it mean the brand never builds the thread-to-thread sensor?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INLINE_CLEARER_QUANTUM explains the winder-mounted clearer that checks the yarn thread-to-thread 100% in-line, records and cuts/splices faults, and logs them, and concludes that the sensing-and-grading the owner imagines already ships on the spinner's machine

competency_questions.question: What incoming AQL inspection does the brand actually own, and what does the inspector check?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INCOMING_AQL_INSPECTION specifies the ISO-2859-1 sampling plan with apparel acceptance levels (Critical 0 / Major 2.5 / Minor 4.0), the near-zero capital (inspector, light box, tape, written standard), and the measurement/seam-linking/visual-defect/label checks, and states that QC without willingness to reject is theatre

competency_questions.question: Which finished-garment lab tests does the brand buy rather than own, and what pass thresholds go into the PO?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FINISHED_GARMENT_LAB_TESTS names pilling grade (ISO 12945-1, >=3-4 post-wash), dimensional stability/shrinkage, spirality, colour fastness, fibre composition, and a discrete Uster evenness spot-check, with the ~$30-250/lot estimate and the per-sample Uster run held UNKNOWN, routed to a third-party lab

competency_questions.question: Is the owner's 'thread-checker' real, buildable, and worth it, decomposed by layer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THREAD_CHECKER_VERDICT decomposes the idea into sense-yarn, sense-knit, grade, and code-back layers, marks the first three as buy-via-PO (already exist, six-figure metrology moat), and isolates the code-back loop as the one cheap ownable sliver

competency_questions.question: How is the supplier-accountability code-back loop built, what does it cost, and what makes its leverage conditional?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CODEBACK_ACCOUNTABILITY_LOOP specifies logging each lot's grade to a scorecard and emitting a grade-code/QR to the named spinner at ~$0-5k estimate, conditions its leverage on a numeric PO spec, willingness to reject, and order size, and distinguishes it from the consumer-facing digital product passport

competency_questions.question: Where does AI vision knit-defect detection genuinely help, and where is the cited accuracy hype?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AI_VISION_DEFECT_SCAN places vision as a cheap L2 fabric-defect screening layer that assists rather than replaces the inspector, and binds the 91-96% accuracy figures as dataset-specific (TILDA/woven/jacquard) and UNKNOWN on our acrylic/blend knits until validated on pre-production samples

competency_questions.question: How is AI-vision accuracy validated on our own fabrics before any vision or thread-checker claim is believed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VISION_VALIDATION_GATE requires a labelled dataset of our defects built from pre-production-sample swatches and a measured accuracy on our acrylic/blend constructions, names the dataset (not the camera) as the true cost, and holds that cost/lead-time UNKNOWN

competency_questions.question: What does the brand RUN versus what does it DEMAND, and how is that boundary drawn against the ~$1-2.50/garment yarn input?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OWN_DEMAND_BUY_BOUNDARY assigns AQL inspection and the lab spot-check budget to RUN, the USTER cert and clearer to DEMAND, and the sensing-and-grading device to NEVER-OWN, justified by the yarn input being ~$1-2.50/garment against six-figure metrology capital

competency_questions.question: How is every QC cost, throughput, and accuracy figure stated honestly without fake precision, and which numbers stay UNKNOWN blockers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QC_HONESTY_DISCIPLINE tags each money/performance claim FACT, ESTIMATE (method+basis+confidence, literal word estimate), or UNKNOWN, names the genuinely-missing numbers (per-lot lab quote near Ludhiana, per-sample Uster run, vision accuracy on our knits, vision-dataset cost, Ludhiana AQL man-day rate, whether spinners act on a code) as blockers, and never fabricates

competency_questions.question: How does the brand sequence QC cheapest-first and review it on what triggers without over-promising a magic device?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QC_SEQUENCE_PLAN orders NOW (PO spec + cert + AQL + lab spot-check + code-back loop), LATER (used inspection rig or validated vision), and NEVER (own a tester, build a clearer, build the sensor); QC_REVIEW_LOOP sets review triggers (return-rate spike, chronic out-of-spec spinner, new construction, validated vision accuracy) that re-run the plan

glossary.definition: The global benchmark that grades a yarn parameter against world production: '25% USTER' means better than 75% of world output on that parameter, lower percentile = better; the common PO language ('must meet 25% USTER on CVm% and IPI') and the moat that makes a home-built grade non-credible.

The off-line laboratory evenness tester (capacitive + optical) that measures CVm%, IPI, hairiness, count-CV, and tenacity and grades them against USTER STATISTICS; six-figure-USD-class capital [price band ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN] that lives on the spinner's floor and is demanded via the PO, never owned by a micro-brand.

The clearer mounted on the spinner's winder that checks the yarn thread-to-thread 100% in-line, records every fault, and cuts and re-splices defects automatically while logging them; it is literally 'check the yarn thread-to-thread and record it,' already productised on the supplier's machine.

Coefficient of variation of mass per unit length (%); the headline yarn-evenness number, lower = more even, the figure a PO clause anchors on alongside IPI; uneven yarn streaks fabric and causes knitting stops and defects.

Thin places (-50%) + thick places (+50%) + neps (+200%) per 1000 m at standard sensitivities; the point-defect cleanliness number specified alongside CVm% in the PO, with high IPI predicting visible faults and knitting stops.

The ISO 2859-1 / ANSI-ASQ Z1.4 statistical sampling plan: pull a lot-sized sample, count defects, accept or reject the whole batch on the count; apparel defaults Critical 0 / Major 2.5 / Minor 4.0; the one QC gate a micro-brand genuinely owns, near-zero capital.

A 1-5 lab wear-test rating (ICI pilling box ISO 12945-1, Martindale, or random tumble; 5 = no pill, 1 = severe) that is the objective test behind any anti-pill claim and the acceptance gate on the #1 post-purchase return driver for acrylic/blend knits; demand >=3-4 after >=1 home wash.

Linking joins panel edges loop-to-loop for a flat near-invisible stretchy seam, the defining quality step of fully-fashioned sweaters; mock-linking imitates the look without true loop-to-loop registration, faster and cheaper; the incoming inspector must distinguish them because they carry the quality-price story.

The buyer-to-supplier accountability instrument the owner's 'thread-checker' actually reduces to: log each lot's grade to a scorecard and emit a grade-code/QR to the named spinner ('here is how lot #47 scored on CVm%, IPI, pilling'); ~$0-5k [ESTIMATE], software glue on a numeric PO, distinct from a sensing machine.

The binding rule that cited 91-96% / >95% computer-vision knit-defect accuracies come from specific datasets (TILDA, woven and jacquard fabrics) and do NOT transfer to our acrylic/blend stockinette and rib knits untested; accuracy on our fabrics is UNKNOWN until validated on pre-production-sample swatches, and vision assists the human inspector rather than replacing him.

nodes.definition: Pin down, for this brand's specific acrylic/blend construction, which defect dominates returns and which the QC plan must protect first: pilling is the #1 post-purchase return driver for short-staple acrylic/blend knits [FACT-class per SCOPE_GLOSSARY sec 1], followed by knit-fabric defects (holes, dropped stitches, barre/streaks, shade mismatch, float problems on jacquard backs), yarn-evenness faults (thin/thick/neps that streak fabric and stop knitting), construction failures (skew/spirality from unbalanced singles twist, mock-linking masquerading as linking), and dimensional instability (shrinkage after the customer washes). Each defect is mapped to the layer where it is caught (yarn, knit, finished-garment), making this profile the raw input that bounds every demand/run/buy choice downstream.

included: the dominant return driver (pilling) and the ranked defect set
mapping each defect to its QC layer
likelihood-times-return-cost ranking
excluded: choosing a specific test or supplier

pros.claim: Naming pilling as the dominant return driver focuses QC spend on the test (pilling grade) and design levers (fibre, twist, gauge, finish) that actually cut returns
pros.example: a brand that ranks pilling first writes a pilling-grade acceptance threshold into the PO before chasing a marginal CVm% improvement the customer never feels

cons.claim: Over-fixating on the single dominant defect can let a lower-frequency but high-severity defect (a shade-mismatched lot, a skewed seam) slip the gate
cons.example: a brand optimizing pilling grade while a barre-streaked dye lot ships and draws a cluster of returns

failure_modes: importing another fibre's defect profile so the wrong defect is protected (e.g. cashmere's shed onto an acrylic line)
treating evenness-class yarn faults as the brand's problem when they are the spinner's to clear in-line
acceptance_tests: the profile names pilling as the dominant return driver and ranks at least four more defects by return risk, each mapped to the yarn, knit, or finished-garment layer
revisit_triggers: the brand changes fibre blend, construction, or gauge
a return-rate analysis surfaces a previously minor defect as the binding driver

base.update_signal: the fibre, construction, or dominant defect-and-return driver changes

nodes.definition: Separate the three layers where a sweater's quality is decided, because the brand's leverage differs completely at each and confusing them is the single most expensive QC mistake a small brand makes. Layer 1, yarn quality (evenness, imperfections, strength), happens in the spinner's lab and winder on USTER-class capital the spinner owns, so the brand DEMANDS it in the PO and never owns it. Layer 2, knit-fabric quality (defects in the knitted panel), happens on the knitter's floor on an inspection frame the knitter owns, so the brand DEMANDS it and explores cheap vision only later. Layer 3, finished-garment quality (measurements, seams, finish, labels), happens on the brand's incoming-goods table on a person plus a tape plus a light, so the brand OWNS this as its real QC. This model is the spine: sense-and-grade is the supplier's; finished-garment AQL is the brand's; lab confirmation is bought.

included: the three layers and who owns the machine at each
the demand/explore/own posture per layer
the rule that the brain owns only the finished-garment layer
excluded: the specific PO clause numbers (own node)

pros.claim: A three-layer model stops the brand from trying to own metrology that belongs on the supplier's floor and from neglecting the one layer it can actually own
pros.example: a founder who internalizes the model budgets an inspector and a lab spot-check instead of pricing a tester they could never justify

cons.claim: A clean three-layer split can understate that real Ludhiana job-work is fragmented across many micro-units, so 'the knitter' and 'the spinner' may be several uncoordinated vendors
cons.example: assuming one knitter owns an inspection frame when the panel passes through three job-workers none of whom inspect

failure_modes: collapsing the layers and trying to test yarn evenness on the incoming table
neglecting the finished-garment layer because the PO 'already covered quality'
acceptance_tests: the model names all three layers with the machine owner and the demand/explore/own posture at each, and states that the brand owns only the finished-garment layer
revisit_triggers: the make-vs-buy boundary shifts (the brand starts owning a knitting or finishing step)
a fragmented job-work chain breaks the one-owner-per-layer assumption

base.update_signal: the layer ownership or the make-vs-buy boundary changes

nodes.definition: Draw the binding boundary between what the brand RUNS, what it DEMANDS of suppliers, and what it BUYS as a service, justified by the economics: the yarn input is roughly $1-2.50/garment [ESTIMATE, from the yarn deep-dive], against which six-figure sensing-and-grading capital is grossly disproportionate. RUN: human incoming AQL garment inspection (near-zero capital) plus the willingness to reject a lot. DEMAND (via the PO): the USTER evenness certificate, the in-line clearer already on the spinner's winder, the numeric CVm%/IPI/hairiness/tenacity/count/composition spec, and the knitter's panel inspection. BUY (third-party): the finished-garment lab tests (pilling, shrinkage, spirality, fastness, composition, a discrete Uster spot-check) at ~$30-250/lot [ESTIMATE]. NEVER-OWN: the USTER Tester 6, a yarn clearer, or a home-built sensing-and-grading thread-checker. The economics alone settle the own-vs-demand question.

included: the RUN / DEMAND / BUY / NEVER-OWN assignment per QC capability
the ~$1-2.50/garment-input economic justification
the disproportionality test against six-figure capital
excluded: the build of the code-back loop (own node)

pros.claim: An explicit run/demand/buy/never-own boundary prevents both over-capitalizing on metrology and under-investing in the ownable inspection gate
pros.example: a brand that places the tester in NEVER-OWN and AQL in RUN spends on an inspector and a lab budget proportionate to a $1-2.50/garment input

cons.claim: The boundary assumes the supplier can actually produce the demanded cert, which a true Ludhiana micro-spinner may not, shifting a demanded item into a bought one
cons.example: a micro-spinner with no tester forcing the brand to pay for a third-party evenness run it expected the supplier to supply

failure_modes: sliding a NEVER-OWN item (a tester, a clearer) into RUN because a demo rig looked cheap
demanding a cert from a supplier structurally unable to produce it and getting nothing
acceptance_tests: each QC capability is assigned to RUN, DEMAND, BUY, or NEVER-OWN with the economic rationale tying the assignment to the ~$1-2.50/garment yarn input
revisit_triggers: the yarn-input cost or order volume moves materially
a supplier's ability to self-certify changes the demand-vs-buy split

base.update_signal: the yarn-input economics or the supplier self-certification reality changes

nodes.definition: Establish USTER STATISTICS as the benchmark every yarn-quality clause and certificate is graded against: a global percentile where '25% USTER' means better than 75% of world production on that parameter and lower percentile = better [FACT, Uster Technologies methodology]. For a mainstream-to-premium acrylic/blend sweater the right tier is <=25% USTER on both CVm% and IPI [FACT for the parameter definitions; ESTIMATE-MED that 25% is the right tier for our product]; the brand does NOT pay for 5% USTER on mass acrylic, which buys a fineness the customer never feels and prices the lot out. This percentile anchor is what makes the PO number credible and what a home-built grade can never replicate, because the benchmark is Uster's decades-deep metrology moat, not a reading a demo rig can produce.

included: the USTER percentile benchmark and what 25% USTER means
the <=25% USTER tier choice for acrylic/blend and the don't-over-tighten rule
why the benchmark is non-replicable by a home rig
excluded: the full multi-parameter PO clause (own node)

pros.claim: Anchoring the spec to a published percentile gives the PO a credible, supplier-recognized number instead of an invented threshold
pros.example: specifying <=25% USTER on CVm% and IPI that any integrated spinner reads the same way, versus a DIY 'evenness score' no spinner honours

cons.claim: A percentile tier is product-specific, and a mis-set tier either over-prices the lot (too tight) or ships streaky fabric (too loose)
cons.example: demanding 5% USTER on a value acrylic count and pricing the order beyond what the line can recover

failure_modes: copying a premium-count percentile onto a mass acrylic count and pricing the lot out
treating a home rig's reading as if it were USTER-benchmarked
acceptance_tests: the anchor states what 25% USTER means, sets <=25% USTER as the acrylic/blend tier on CVm% and IPI, and explains why not to over-tighten to 5%
revisit_triggers: the product tier moves up toward premium or down toward value
Uster updates its STATISTICS benchmark edition

base.update_signal: the product tier or the USTER STATISTICS edition changes

nodes.definition: Write the numeric yarn-quality clause into the purchase order, because the brand's QC starts as a contract number, not a machine, and this is the cheapest, highest-leverage QC it does. The clause states: CVm% (mass evenness) and IPI (thin -50% / thick +50% / neps +200% per 1000 m), both demanded <=25% USTER for mainstream-to-premium acrylic/blend [FACT for definitions; ESTIMATE-MED for the tier]; a hairiness (H/S3) ceiling, because too-high hairiness drives pilling, the #1 return risk; a tenacity/elongation floor so the yarn does not break in knitting (downtime) or in seams; the actual count (Ne/Nm) plus a count-CV tolerance so GSM and shade do not drift between batches; and the exact fibre-composition ratio (e.g. 70/30 acrylic/wool), which double-duties as a customs-duty-misdeclaration guard since the care label and the HTS line must match the yarn. The spinner must then prove they hit it, via cert or paid lab run.

included: the full CVm%/IPI/hairiness/tenacity/count-CV/composition clause
the pilling-and-duty rationale behind hairiness and composition
the demand that the spinner prove the spec

pros.claim: A precise numeric clause converts QC from an after-the-fact inspection into a pre-committed contract the supplier shares risk on, at zero capital cost
pros.example: a PO line '<=25% USTER CVm% and IPI, H<=ceiling, 70/30 acrylic/wool +/- tolerance' that the spinner must certify before shipping

cons.claim: An over-stuffed or mis-tiered clause can make the lot unquotable to a micro-spinner or demand a fineness the product never needs
cons.example: stacking 5% USTER, a tight hairiness ceiling, and a narrow count-CV that no target Ludhiana micro-spinner can quote

failure_modes: specifying numbers with no cert mechanism to verify them, so the clause is unenforceable
letting the composition ratio in the clause drift from the care label and HTS line, creating a duty-misdeclaration exposure
acceptance_tests: the clause specifies CVm%, IPI, a hairiness ceiling, a tenacity/elongation floor, count plus count-CV tolerance, and the exact fibre-composition ratio, each with its rationale and a verification path
revisit_triggers: the product tier, blend ratio, or target count changes
a duty/HTS reclassification changes the composition declaration

base.update_signal: the blend ratio, count, tier, or duty declaration changes

nodes.definition: Describe the USTER TESTER 6, the global off-line laboratory evenness tester (capacitive + optical) that measures exactly CVm%, IPI, hairiness, count-CV, and tenacity and grades them against USTER STATISTICS [FACT, uster.com TESTER 6 datasheets]. Its price is six-figure-USD class; the exact list price is [UNKNOWN] because Uster does not publish it, reconciled to a wide band of ~$80k-400k+ [ESTIMATE, LOW confidence]. The brand will never own one. The certificate it produces is obtained one of two ways: a large integrated group (e.g. Vardhman/Nahar/Sportking class) self-tests and hands over a USTER report, or a target Ludhiana micro-spinner that owns no tester at all forces the cert to come from a third-party lab run the brand pays for. Which path applies is [ESTIMATE, MED-HIGH that micro-spinners cannot self-test] and decides whether the PO cert is supplier-supplied or brand-bought.

included: what the Tester 6 measures and grades
the six-figure price held as a wide ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN
the two certificate-acquisition paths (integrated self-test vs paid third-party)

pros.claim: Knowing the tester and its certificate paths lets the brand talk to the spinner credibly and route the cert correctly without ever owning the capital
pros.example: a buyer who knows Vardhman-class groups self-test asks for the USTER report directly, but books a third-party run when sourcing from a micro-spinner

cons.claim: The price is a wide low-confidence band, so any own-vs-rent math built on the exact number is fragile
cons.example: trying to compute a precise payback on owning a tester from a $80k-400k band that spans 5x

failure_modes: assuming a micro-spinner can hand over a USTER cert when it owns no tester
treating the six-figure price as precise enough to model an ownership decision the economics already foreclose
acceptance_tests: the node states what the Tester 6 measures, holds the price as a six-figure ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN, and routes the certificate through either an integrated self-tester or a paid third-party lab
revisit_triggers: a real Tester 6 list/used quote becomes available
the chosen spinner's self-test capability is confirmed or refuted

base.update_signal: a tester price quote or the spinner's self-test capability is confirmed

nodes.definition: Describe the USTER QUANTUM in-line yarn clearer mounted on the spinner's winder: it checks the yarn thread-to-thread, 100% in-line, records every fault, cuts and re-splices defects automatically, and logs to the cloud [FACT, uster.com QUANTUM]. This is literally 'check the yarn thread-to-thread and record it,' already productised, and it lives on the spinner's machine, not the brand's. The realization to internalize: the owner's instinct to grade every bit of thread and record it is correct and already shipping as a yarn clearer, so the brand does NOT build the part that senses and grades; it demands the spinner already runs it and hands over the certificate. Generic clearers from other vendors fill the same role; the category, not the brand, is the point. This node is the factual spine of the don't-build-the-sensor verdict.

included: the winder-mounted thread-to-thread clearer and its record/cut/splice/log function
the conclusion that the sensing-and-grading already ships on the supplier's machine
the clearer category beyond the one brand
excluded: the code-back loop the brand can build (own node)

pros.claim: Recognizing that thread-to-thread sensing already ships in-line on the spinner's winder kills the temptation to reinvent it and redirects effort to demanding the log
pros.example: a brand that asks for the clearer's fault log per lot instead of prototyping its own thread sensor

cons.claim: A target micro-spinner may run an older or no clearer, so the in-line log the brand wants to demand may not exist to hand over
cons.example: a small winder with a basic clearer that does not export a per-lot fault log

failure_modes: building a thread-to-thread sensor that duplicates a clearer already on the supplier's floor
assuming every spinner's clearer exports a usable per-lot log when a micro-unit's may not
acceptance_tests: the node describes the in-line clearer's thread-to-thread record/cut/splice/log function and concludes the brand demands rather than builds the sensing-and-grading layer
revisit_triggers: the chosen spinner's clearer generation or log-export capability is confirmed
a cheaper in-line sensing option emerges that changes the build-vs-demand call

base.update_signal: the spinner's clearer capability or a new in-line sensing option changes

nodes.definition: Set up the incoming AQL inspection, the one QC the brand actually owns: when garments arrive, a human inspects a statistical sample against a written defect standard, at near-zero capital (an inspector, a light box, a tape measure, and a written standard). AQL (ISO 2859-1 / ANSI-ASQ Z1.4) sizes the sample to the lot, counts defects, and accepts or rejects the whole batch on the count [FACT]. The apparel acceptance levels are Critical 0 (zero tolerance, anything unsafe/unsellable), Major 2.5 (defects a customer would return for), and Minor 4.0 (cosmetic flaws) [FACT, QIMA/ASQ apparel defaults]. The inspector checks measurements against the tech pack within tolerance, seam/linking quality (true linking vs mock-link/overlock), visual defects (holes, dropped stitches, barre, shade mismatch, loose ends, jacquard float problems), and labels/care (composition matching the yarn cert and the duty declaration). This step closes the loop the PO spec opened: the demanded numbers and bought lab tests only have teeth if the brand samples, grades, and rejects on arrival. QC without willingness to reject a lot is theatre.

included: the AQL sampling plan and Critical 0 / Major 2.5 / Minor 4.0 levels
the near-zero-capital inspection kit
the measurement/seam/visual/label checklist and the reject discipline
excluded: the lab tests that need equipment (own node)

pros.claim: An owned AQL gate with a real reject decision is the brand's only true quality control and costs almost nothing in capital
pros.example: an inspector pulling a Z1.4 sample, finding Major defects above 2.5, and rejecting the lot before it reaches customers

cons.claim: AQL is only as good as the inspector's skill and the brand's willingness to actually reject, both of which a thin team can compromise under shipping pressure

the lab tests confirm the spinner met the PO clause and add the garment-level acceptance thresholds
the pilling gate is the highest-priority specialization of the bought lab-test set
the already-shipping in-line clearer is the fact that grounds the don't-build-the-sensor verdict
the never-own boundary drives the build-only-the-loop conclusion of the verdict
the verdict isolates the code-back loop as the one buildable sliver the loop node then specifies
the numeric PO spec is the grade-against substrate without which the code-back loop has no teeth
the knit-fabric defect set (holes, dropped stitches, streaks) defines what vision could screen for
the dataset-transfer caveat forces the validation gate before any vision claim is believed
the lab-cost band is a primary claim the honesty discipline must tag as an estimate
the six-figure tester price is the headline wide-estimate the honesty discipline governs
the recurring lab-test cost line is the main QC budget exposure the risk node tracks
the UNKNOWN cost blockers the honesty discipline names are the items that could swing the QC budget
the code-back scorecard is the detector that flags the chronically out-of-spec spinner a backup answers
the tracked cost-and-failure exposure is what the per-dependency backup plan mitigates
a rejected lot at the AQL gate triggers the backup-supplier substitution
the PO spec is the NOW first step of the cheapest-first sequence
the code-back loop is the NOW buildable sliver folded into the sequence
the validation gate sets the validate-before-vision condition on the LATER step of the sequence
the per-dependency backups are folded into the consolidated QC operating plan
the review loop watches the consolidated sequence and triggers re-planning
the pilling gate is the QC test a pilling-return spike routes back to re-tighten

edges.resolution_rule: run AQL on every lot as the near-zero-capital owned gate; buy the lab panel per lot for the defects the eye cannot grade (pilling, shrinkage, fastness, evenness), rotating non-critical tests across lots while keeping pilling on every lot

edges.why_related: vision as a screening layer competes with the human inspector for the accept/reject authority, and treating it as a replacement undercuts the owned gate
edges.resolution_rule: keep the human inspector as the final accept/reject authority; use vision only as a validated screening assist that triages panels, never as the replacement, until accuracy on our fabrics is measured

edges.why_related: tighter USTER percentiles protect quality but can make the lot unquotable to a micro-spinner or over-price it, pulling against the clause being filled
edges.resolution_rule: set each parameter to its tier optimum (<=25% USTER on CVm% and IPI, a hairiness ceiling that controls pilling, a count-CV tolerance that holds shade); never tighten to a level a target Ludhiana micro-spinner cannot quote, and reserve 5% USTER for a genuinely premium count only

edges.why_related: the code-back loop's leverage to discipline a spinner competes with the cost and feasibility of qualifying a backup that gives the threat teeth, especially for a micro-order
edges.resolution_rule: build the near-free code-back loop regardless; qualify a backup spinner only once order volume is large enough that a second spinner will engage and the scorecard's drop-threat is credible, otherwise treat the loop as a selection record not a live threat

edges.why_related: a too-loose pilling acceptance threshold causally raises the pilling-return rate the feedback loop then detects

conflict_axes.name: own_vs_demand_qc_capital
conflict_axes.description: Owning sensing-and-grading metrology gives control but is six-figure capital disproportionate to a ~$1-2.50/garment input; demanding it via the PO keeps the capital on the supplier floor at the cost of dependence on the supplier's instruments.
poles: demand it via the PO and never own
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never own the tester or clearer; demand the cert via the PO and buy a third-party run when a micro-spinner cannot self-certify

conflict_axes.name: human_inspector_vs_ai_vision
conflict_axes.description: A skilled human reading seam/linking and shade is the standard for a small premium line, while AI vision adds tireless consistency but is unvalidated on our fabrics and tempts a replace-the-human error.
poles: keep the human as final authority
lean on AI vision for consistency
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: human is the final accept/reject; vision is a validated screening assist only, never the replacement, until measured on our knits

conflict_axes.name: spec_tightness_vs_quotability
conflict_axes.description: Tighter USTER percentiles and parameter ceilings protect quality but can price the lot out or make it unquotable to a target micro-spinner.
poles: loosen to keep the lot quotable
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set each dial to its tier optimum (<=25% USTER for mainstream-to-premium acrylic); reserve 5% USTER for a genuinely premium count

conflict_axes.name: build_the_loop_vs_build_the_sensor
conflict_axes.description: The owner's thread-checker instinct splits into a cheap buildable code-back loop and an expensive don't-build sensing-and-grading device that reinvents a metrology moat.
poles: build only the cheap code-back loop
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: build only the L4 code-back loop on a numeric PO spine; never build the L1/L2/L3 sensor that already ships on the supplier's floor

conflict_axes.name: test_coverage_vs_qc_cost
conflict_axes.description: Running the full lab panel on every lot maximizes coverage but the recurring ~$30-250/lot cost can outpace a micro-capsule's thin margin, while under-testing re-exposes the costly defects.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep pilling on every lot, rotate non-critical lab tests across lots, and right-size the panel to the dominant return driver

conflict_axes.name: single_spinner_simplicity_vs_qc_resilience
conflict_axes.description: Single-sourcing the spinner simplifies the relationship and earns engagement but concentrates the dominant pilling-and-evenness risk with no qualified alternative.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: qualify a backup spinner for the dominant cost-and-return dependency once order volume makes a second spinner engage; keep the code-back scorecard as the trigger

conflict_axes.name: demanded_cert_vs_micro_spinner_capability
conflict_axes.description: Demanding a USTER cert in the PO is the cheapest QC, but a target Ludhiana micro-spinner may own no tester, forcing the cert into a brand-paid third-party run.
poles: demand the cert from the spinner
pay for a third-party lab cert
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: demand the cert from integrated groups that self-test; budget a brand-paid third-party run when sourcing from a micro-spinner that cannot self-certify

conflict_axes.name: validate_now_vs_defer_vision
conflict_axes.description: Validating vision on our fabrics now costs an UNKNOWN dataset-build effort, while deferring vision keeps QC cheap but forgoes the one brand-cheap defect-detection frontier.
poles: defer vision until volume justifies it
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: defer vision to the LATER step and validate on PPS swatches only at proven repeat volume on a style; never adopt an unvalidated accuracy figure

conflict_axes.name: estimate_usefulness_vs_fake_precision
conflict_axes.description: A usable QC cost band needs a number, but stating a wide estimate or an UNKNOWN blocker as fake-precise misleads the downstream cost model.
poles: state a precise number for usability
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: give the band as a labeled estimate with confidence and a confirmation path, and keep the genuinely-missing number an explicit UNKNOWN blocker

edge_cases.description: A target Ludhiana micro-spinner owns no USTER tester and cannot supply the cert the PO demands
edge_cases.trigger: the PO demands a USTER cert from a spinner that does not self-test
edge_cases.mitigation: route the cert through a brand-paid third-party lab evenness run and budget it as a bought, not demanded, item

edge_cases.description: A supplier substitutes mock-linking for the true linking the PO specified and paid for
edge_cases.trigger: an incoming lot has mock-linked seams on a fully-fashioned true-linking spec
edge_cases.mitigation: train the inspector to distinguish true linking from mock-link and overlock and reject the downgraded construction

edge_cases.description: An anti-pill claim does not survive the wash test and a low-pilling-grade lot ships and returns
edge_cases.trigger: a lot grades below 3-4 after one home wash on a spec demanding >=3-4
edge_cases.mitigation: make the post-wash pilling grade a hard reject gate and re-tighten the PO hairiness/twist clause that drives pilling

edge_cases.description: A vision model validated on TILDA woven/jacquard data is deployed on our acrylic/blend rib knits where colour noise breaks it
edge_cases.trigger: a cited 91-96% accuracy is trusted without validation on our fabrics
edge_cases.mitigation: treat any accuracy figure as marketing until measured on our PPS swatches, and keep the human inspector as the authority

edge_cases.description: The code-back loop is built but the spinner ignores the returned grade because the order is too small to matter
edge_cases.trigger: a micro-capsule emits a grade code a large spinner has no incentive to act on
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the loop as a selection record that informs which spinner to re-order from rather than a live threat, until order volume gives it teeth

edge_cases.description: The dominant pilling-driving spinner is single-sourced and ships a chronically out-of-spec lot with no backup qualified
edge_cases.trigger: the only spinner runs out of spec and no second spinner is pre-qualified
edge_cases.mitigation: pre-qualify a backup spinner for the dominant cost-and-return dependency and switch on the scorecard trigger

edge_cases.description: AQL is run but the brand waves a borderline lot through to hit a drop date, turning the gate into theatre
edge_cases.trigger: a Major-defect count above 2.5 is accepted under shipping pressure
edge_cases.mitigation: pre-commit the reject rule and hold it; QC without willingness to reject is theatre

edge_cases.description: The full lab panel is run on every small lot and the recurring cost outpaces the capsule's thin margin
edge_cases.trigger: every parameter is tested on every low-volume lot
edge_cases.mitigation: keep pilling on every lot and rotate non-critical tests across lots to right-size the panel to the dominant return driver

edge_cases.description: A QC cost figure is stated as fake-precise when the real near-Ludhiana quote is UNKNOWN
edge_cases.trigger: a per-lot lab or per-sample Uster cost is quoted without the estimate-or-UNKNOWN label
edge_cases.mitigation: give every cost as a labeled estimate with confidence and a confirmation path, and keep the genuinely-missing number an explicit UNKNOWN blocker

edge_cases.description: The fibre composition in the PO clause drifts from the care label and HTS line, creating a duty-misdeclaration exposure
edge_cases.trigger: the blend ratio specified, labelled, and declared do not match
edge_cases.mitigation: verify composition by lab test and keep the clause, care label, and HTS declaration identical

edge_cases.description: A second spinner is named as backup but never actually qualified, so it fails when the primary is dropped
edge_cases.trigger: the backup spinner is called on for the first time during a real outage
edge_cases.mitigation: qualify the backup with a real sample-and-cert run before relying on it, not at the moment of failure

edge_cases.description: Return data is collected without a reason code, so the QC gate to re-tighten cannot be identified
edge_cases.trigger: returns accrue with no per-return defect reason
edge_cases.mitigation: capture a return reason on every return and map each reason to the QC layer and test that should have caught it

workflow.description: Name pilling as the dominant return driver and rank the knit/yarn/construction defects by return risk, each mapped to its QC layer
workflow.gate: the dominant return driver is named and at least four more defects are ranked and layer-mapped

workflow.action: Fix the three-layer QC ownership model
workflow.description: Separate yarn/knit/finished-garment layers and assign demand/explore/own posture per layer
workflow.gate: all three layers have a machine owner and a demand/explore/own posture, with the brand owning only the finished-garment layer

workflow.description: Assign each QC capability to RUN, DEMAND, BUY, or NEVER-OWN against the ~$1-2.50/garment input
workflow.gate: every QC capability is assigned with the economic rationale tying it to the yarn input

workflow.action: Write the numeric PO yarn-quality clause
workflow.description: Specify CVm%, IPI, hairiness ceiling, tenacity floor, count-CV tolerance, and composition anchored to <=25% USTER
workflow.gate: the clause states all six parameters with rationale and a verification path

workflow.action: Route the USTER certificate and confirm the clearer
workflow.description: Hold the tester as a six-figure never-own item, route the cert via self-test or third-party lab, and confirm the in-line clearer on the spinner's winder
workflow.gate: the cert is routed by spinner capability and the in-line clearer is confirmed as supplier-owned

workflow.action: Stand up the owned incoming AQL inspection
workflow.description: Set the AQL plan with Critical 0 / Major 2.5 / Minor 4.0, the near-zero-capital kit, and the measurement/seam/visual/label checklist with a reject rule
workflow.gate: the AQL plan, acceptance levels, checklist, and explicit reject rule exist

workflow.action: Buy the finished-garment lab tests with PO thresholds
workflow.description: Route pilling, shrinkage, spirality, fastness, composition, and a discrete Uster spot-check to a third-party lab with thresholds and the cost estimate
workflow.gate: the test panel with thresholds, the ~$30-250/lot estimate, and the UNKNOWN per-sample Uster run are stated

workflow.action: Decide the thread-checker and build only the code-back loop
workflow.description: Decompose the thread-checker into four layers, buy the first three via PO, and build the ~$0-5k code-back loop on the numeric PO spine
workflow.gate: the four-layer verdict holds and only the code-back loop is built, with its three leverage conditions stated

workflow.action: Place AI vision and gate it behind validation
workflow.description: Position vision as an assisting L2 screening layer and require a measured accuracy on our PPS swatches before any claim is believed
workflow.gate: vision is an assist-not-replace screening layer and its accuracy on our fabrics is required before belief

workflow.action: Tag every QC claim and name the UNKNOWN blockers
workflow.description: Tag each money/performance/regulation claim FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN and list the genuinely-missing blockers
workflow.gate: every claim is tagged and the named UNKNOWN blockers are listed, off-paper material mechanism-not-accusation

workflow.action: Add per-dependency backups and assemble the cheapest-first sequence
workflow.description: Qualify a backup per critical QC dependency and order QC into NOW/LATER/NEVER with cost tags
workflow.gate: each critical dependency has a backup and QC is ordered NOW/LATER/NEVER with cost tags

workflow.action: Set the review cadence and the return-data feedback
workflow.description: Define the review cadence and material-change triggers routing back to the defect profile and PO spec, with return-reason-to-gate feedback
workflow.gate: a cadence and trigger list routing to DEFECT_RISK_PROFILE and the PO spec exist, with returns mapped to gates

dominance_rules.rule: Never-own dominates any urge to build or buy the sensing-and-grading device
dominance_rules.rationale: thread-to-thread sensing and benchmark grading already ship on the supplier's floor as six-figure capital disproportionate to a ~$1-2.50/garment input; a home rig can demo a reading but cannot credibly grade against USTER STATISTICS
dominance_rules.trigger: any plan to own a tester, build a clearer, or build the thread-checker sensor
dominance_rules.action: block the build, demand the cert via the PO, and build only the cheap code-back loop

dominance_rules.rule: Validation-on-our-fabrics dominates any vision or thread-checker accuracy claim
dominance_rules.rationale: cited 91-96% accuracies are dataset-specific to woven/jacquard and do not transfer to our acrylic/blend knits untested
dominance_rules.trigger: a vision or AI accuracy figure is about to drive a QC decision
dominance_rules.action: treat it as marketing until measured on our PPS swatches and keep the human inspector as the authority

dominance_rules.rule: Willingness-to-reject dominates the cost of holding a lot
dominance_rules.rationale: AQL and the PO spec only have teeth if the brand actually rejects out-of-spec lots; without it the whole gate is theatre
dominance_rules.trigger: a borderline lot is about to be accepted under shipping pressure
dominance_rules.action: hold the pre-committed reject rule and reject the lot

dominance_rules.rule: Honesty labeling dominates any QC cost, throughput, or accuracy figure
dominance_rules.rationale: a fake-precise number for a genuinely-UNKNOWN blocker misleads the downstream cost model and violates the honesty discipline
dominance_rules.action: express it as a labeled estimate with confidence and a confirmation path, or as an explicit UNKNOWN blocker

dominance_rules.rule: The pilling gate dominates marginal evenness gains
dominance_rules.rationale: pilling is the #1 post-purchase return driver, so a post-wash pilling threshold protects more margin than a marginal CVm% improvement the customer never feels
dominance_rules.trigger: QC effort is about to chase fineness the customer cannot perceive over the dominant return driver
dominance_rules.action: secure the pilling acceptance gate and the hairiness/twist clause first

dominance_rules.rule: A backup for the dominant cost-and-return dependency dominates single-supplier engagement
dominance_rules.rationale: an outage or chronic out-of-spec on the pilling-driving spinner or the linking step strands the line, costing more than the single-source engagement earns
dominance_rules.trigger: the dominant QC dependency is about to be single-sourced
dominance_rules.action: qualify a backup before single-sourcing, once order volume makes a second spinner engage

dominance_rules.rule: The numeric PO spec dominates the code-back loop
dominance_rules.rationale: the code-back loop has no teeth without a numeric PO spec to grade lots against, so the spec must exist first
dominance_rules.trigger: the code-back loop is about to be built before the PO spec is written
dominance_rules.action: write the numeric PO clause first, then build the loop on top of it

dominance_rules.rule: The human inspector dominates AI vision for final accept/reject
dominance_rules.rationale: a skilled human reading seam/linking and shade is still the standard for a small premium line, and vision is a multiplier, not a substitute
dominance_rules.trigger: vision is about to be given final accept/reject authority
dominance_rules.action: keep the human as the final authority and use vision only as a validated screening assist

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the run/demand/buy/never-own boundary before pricing any QC equipment
anti_rework_rules.prevents: pricing or buying metrology that belongs on the supplier floor and disproportionate to a ~$1-2.50/garment input

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the numeric PO yarn-quality clause before building the code-back loop
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a code-back loop with no spec to grade against, so the returned code is meaningless

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm whether the spinner can self-certify before promising a demanded cert
anti_rework_rules.prevents: demanding a USTER cert a micro-spinner cannot supply and stranding the QC gate

anti_rework_rules.rule: Validate vision accuracy on our own PPS swatches before adopting any vision step
anti_rework_rules.prevents: deploying a dataset-specific accuracy figure that does not transfer to our acrylic/blend knits

anti_rework_rules.rule: Train the inspector to distinguish true linking from mock-linking before the first lot
anti_rework_rules.prevents: accepting a downgraded construction on a fully-fashioned true-linking spec

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every QC cost figure estimate-or-UNKNOWN when first written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a planning estimate being quoted downstream as a measured per-lot fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pre-commit the AQL reject rule before the first delivery
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a borderline lot being waved through under shipping pressure, turning the gate into theatre

anti_rework_rules.rule: Qualify a backup spinner or lab before relying on it in an outage
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a named-but-unqualified backup failing the first time it is called on

iteration_protocol.trigger: the brand changes fibre blend, construction, or gauge
iteration_protocol.action: re-profile the dominant defect, re-anchor the PO spec, and re-run the QC sequence

iteration_protocol.trigger: a return-rate reason (especially pilling) climbs past threshold
iteration_protocol.action: map the reason to its gate and re-tighten that test and the PO clause that drives it

iteration_protocol.trigger: the code-back scorecard shows a spinner chronically out-of-spec
iteration_protocol.action: activate the backup spinner, re-qualify the cert path, and update the plan

iteration_protocol.trigger: a real per-lot lab or per-sample Uster quote near Ludhiana lands
iteration_protocol.action: convert the UNKNOWN cost blocker into an estimate and re-cost the QC line

iteration_protocol.trigger: a vision accuracy is measured on our PPS swatches
iteration_protocol.action: re-decide the explore-later vision verdict and, if validated, add it as a screening assist

iteration_protocol.trigger: proven repeat volume on a style is reached
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate the LATER used-rig or validated-vision step and the second-spinner backup

iteration_protocol.trigger: a micro-spinner is found unable to supply a USTER cert
iteration_protocol.action: re-route the cert to a brand-paid third-party run and re-budget it as a bought item

priority_rationale: Foundational defect-profiling, the three-layer ownership model, and the run/demand/buy boundary precede everything because every QC choice depends on knowing the dominant return driver, who owns the machine at each layer, and what the brand can afford to own against a ~$1-2.50/garment input; the PO spec, certificate routing, owned AQL inspection, and bought lab tests build the operating QC; the thread-checker verdict and code-back loop resolve the owner's idea into a don't-build-the-sensor plus a cheap buildable loop; AI vision and its validation gate quarantine the one brand-cheap frontier behind a binding dataset-transfer caveat; honesty discipline, cost-and-failure exposure, and per-dependency backups harden the system into an honestly-costed, resilient gate; the consolidated cheapest-first sequence composes it all, and the review loop plus return-data feedback come last because they watch the whole plan and route material changes back to the foundations.
